text.p: Dutch builder Volker Stevin NV said on Tuesday it was in talks to merge with sector rival Kondor Wessels Groep, creating a combine set to lead the field in Dutch infrastructure and housing construction.

"The boards of Kondor Wessels Groep and Volker Stevin NV announce that discussions are taking place on a full merger of the two companies on equal terms, based upon an expected share exchange of 2.25 shares of Kondor Wessels Groep in one share of Royal Volker Stevin," the companies said in a joint statement.
Shares in both companies surged on the news, seen by analysts as a particular coup for Volker Stevin.
"It's a world class move for Volker," said Konrad Zomer, construction analyst with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"Volker has repeatedly stated in the past it wanted to expand its activities in the Dutch housing market and this will give it the required scale at a single stroke," he said.
Volker Stevin, Dutch market leader in road construction, turns over some 435 million guilders annually in Dutch house building, and was seeking to boost this to some 500-600 million, he said.
Last year Volker booked total turnover of 2.78 billion.
Kondor Wessels' housing turnover amounted to some 285 million guilders annually, Zomer said, making it a "perfect fit" with Volker's ambitions.
"I'm banking on the deal going ahead," he said. "I estimate it will up Volker's profits per share by around 60 guilder cents to 14.80 guilders over the current year.
Lucien van der Linden, construction analyst with Rabo Securities, said he was eager for more information. "I'm pretty sure it will go ahead," he agreed.
"The two companies are a good fit both regionally and in terms of sector. The merged group will occupy a leading position in housing and infrastructure construction."

Economies of scale would render the two companies more competitive and would position them favourably in the run-up to the next century, as foreign builders increasingly sought to muscle in on the healthy Dutch construction market, he said.

"Furthermore the combine will be even better placed to undertake fully-integrated projects involving housing, infrastructure and civil engineering like (the multi-million guilder project to redevelop the Hague suburb of) Voorburg awarded to Volker last year," Van der Linden said.
For its part Kondor Wessels would gain the added financial backbone necessary to ride out a wave of concentration in the Dutch building sector, Zomer said.
Investors on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange cheered the merger news, sending Volker Stevin shares rocketing 13.60 guilders or 7.22 percent to an all-time high of 202.00 guilders.
Kondor Wessels shares closed Tuesday's session up 1.40 guilders at 88.10.
